commentary: Sweden supplementary budget HD01FiU48 cuts fuel taxes by 82 ore/liter for petrol and 319 SEK/m3 for diesel from May through September 2026, reducing both to the EU energy tax directive minimum. This 4.1 billion SEK intervention responds directly to the consumer price pressure Sweden experienced as inflation peaked at 8.5% in 2023 and 8.4% in 2022, before falling to 2.8% in 2024 — yet household energy costs remain politically salient as many Swedish families absorbed multi-year purchasing power losses. With Sweden GDP recovering to 0.82% growth in 2024 after a -0.20% contraction in 2023, the government positions the measure as affordable cost-of-living relief that the improved fiscal position permits. The Nordic comparison adds urgency: Denmark grew at 1.75% in 2024 versus Sweden 0.82%, giving the opposition evidence that Sweden recovery lags neighbours — which the government answers with direct household fuel and energy relief timed to the pre-election period.
